blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Hardware has a lifecycle. A laptop is bought, handed to an employee, used for three or four years, replaced, and eventually recycled or sold. Servers, printers, phones and network equipment all follow similar patterns. A good IT team plans each stage in advance — not at the moment a device actually breaks.

Lifecycle planning makes several things easier. Budgeting becomes predictable: the team knows how many laptops they are going to need next year. Security improves, because old devices are retired before they become vulnerable. Users are happier too: they get working kit on time instead of waiting two weeks for a replacement.

This year, we are going to replace a quarter of the fleet, gradually and invisibly, exactly as we planned in January. Nobody will notice the change — which is exactly the sign that the lifecycle is being managed well.

items.q: According to the text, when does a good IT team plan each stage of the lifecycle?
options: At the moment a device breaks
Only when the budget is approved
items.why: "plans each stage in advance — not at the moment a device actually breaks."

items.q: Why does security improve with lifecycle planning?
options: Because old devices are retired before they become vulnerable
Because users are trained every year
Because devices are encrypted at purchase
items.why: "Security improves, because old devices are retired before they become vulnerable."

items.q: What makes budgeting more predictable, according to the text?
options: The team knows how many laptops they are going to need next year
Every device is bought at the same time
items.why: "the team knows how many laptops they are going to need next year."

items.q: The author says "Nobody will notice the change". This suggests that…
options: the replacement is being kept secret from managers
the new laptops are identical to the old ones
smooth, unnoticed change is a sign of good management
users do not care about their equipment
items.why: Inferência: para o autor, a ausência de ruído é justamente a prova de que o ciclo foi bem gerido.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Predictable budgets are an advantage of lifecycle planning
Replacing devices in stages is worth planning for
Retiring old kit early reduces security risk
The best time to buy a new laptop is after the old one fails
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro defende planejar antes da falha, não esperar o equipamento quebrar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o plano de ciclo de vida à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning, everyone. Before I show you any numbers, I want to be clear about the goal. This year we are going to replace roughly a quarter of the laptop fleet, and if we do it properly, none of you will notice it happening.

Here is how it works. Every device is already tracked in our asset system, so I know exactly which machines are reaching four years of age. Those are the ones going first. We will swap them in small batches, a few each week, always outside working hours. The user arrives on Monday, and the new laptop is simply there, set up and ready.

I am not going to wait for machines to fail. A planned replacement costs us far less than an emergency one, and it protects the data too — every retired device is wiped securely before it leaves the building. The ones that still work will be donated rather than thrown away.

So, to be honest, if this project is a success, it will look like nothing happened at all. That is the point. Any questions before I walk you through the schedule?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Harry's main goal for this year?
options: To replace about a quarter of the laptop fleet without users noticing
To move all machines to a new asset system
To buy laptops for every new employee
To reduce the IT team's headcount
items.why: "we are going to replace roughly a quarter of the laptop fleet… none of you will notice it happening."

items.q: How does Harry decide which machines to replace first?
options: The machines reaching four years of age, tracked in the asset system
The ones that have already failed
items.why: "I know exactly which machines are reaching four years of age. Those are the ones going first."

items.q: Why does Harry refuse to wait for machines to fail?
options: Because failures are impossible to detect
Because a planned replacement costs far less than an emergency one
items.why: "A planned replacement costs us far less than an emergency one, and it protects the data too."

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says "it will look like nothing happened at all"?
options: The laptops will not actually be replaced
A smooth, invisible rollout is the sign of success
Nobody will be told about the plan
The project will probably be cancelled
items.why: Inferência: para Harry, a troca ideal é a que ninguém percebe — a invisibilidade é o objetivo, não um problema.

items.q: What can we infer about Harry's approach to retired devices?
options: He values both data security and sustainability
He keeps them in storage as spares
He returns them to the manufacturer
He sells them immediately to recover cash
items.why: Inferência: ele apaga os dados com segurança (segurança) e doa o que ainda funciona (sustentabilidade).

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We manage the whole hardware lifecycle, from purchase to disposal." The hardware lifecycle is…
options: the price paid for new equipment
the full path of a device from purchase to retirement
the software installed on a machine
the warranty period of a single device
items.why: Hardware lifecycle = ciclo de vida do hardware, da compra ao descarte.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Old servers are ___ before they become a security risk."
items.why: To retire = desativar/aposentar um equipamento antes que vire risco.

items.q: "Every machine is tracked, so demand is predictable." Predictable means…
items.why: Predictable = previsível, fácil de antecipar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We will refresh a quarter of the ___ this year, laptop by laptop."
items.why: Fleet = frota, o conjunto de equipamentos da empresa.

items.q: "Planning each stage in advance avoids emergencies." In advance means…
items.why: In advance = com antecedência, antes de o problema acontecer.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de TI e planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the replacement budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new laptops region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Before we retire a device, we always back up the user's files." To back up means to…
items.why: Back up = fazer cópia de segurança dos dados.

items.q: "The team agreed the schedule but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Old machines are wiped and then phased out of the fleet." To phase out means to…
items.why: Phase out = retirar aos poucos, gradualmente.
